A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GTJM/DSD framework and are readable throughout, including equations, figures, and tables. Both end with references and contain no appendices. Separately referenced supplementary material is not included, so its contents cannot be compared.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic-scene reconstruction results, baseline comparisons, ablations, and sensitivity analyses in Tables 1–3 and associated figures.

after.justification: V2 retains original synthetic experiments and additionally reports real-world reconstruction results and a dynamic blurry-scene comparison.

M1.justification: The core threshold optimization, event supervision, and dynamic-static decomposition procedures remain unchanged. V2 adds an adaptation using blur loss and EDI for dynamic blurry scenes (Section 4.2), although its detailed implementation is deferred to unavailable supplementary material.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates eight synthetic scenes only. V2 retains these and adds four captured scenes—Excavator, Jeep, Flowers, and Eagle—plus dynamic blurry-scene evaluation. This substantially expands coverage to real sensor data and blurred inputs.

E2.justification: The original synthetic comparator set remains unchanged, and the real-world comparison reuses 4D-GS, Deformable-3DGS, and Event-4DGS. V2 additionally evaluates a blur-adapted Deformable-3DGS comparator in Figure 9; Section 4.2 describes extending comparison methods with blur loss and EDI. DE-NeRF remains unevaluated.

E3.justification: V2 introduces real-video evaluation using downsampled training frames and intermediate test frames, alongside the blurry-scene comparison procedure. The existing synthetic training count and PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS/FPS metrics persist. Newly specifying uniform synthetic sampling and intermediate test-frame selection documents the protocol without establishing a changed split or rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds a motion-blur case study testing the adapted method (Figure 9). The GTJM, DSD, and buffer ablations and existing sensitivity analyses remain, although ablation reporting is condensed to averages. Real-world ablations are referenced but their results are absent from the supplied PDF.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2's aggregate ablation scores summarize scenes rather than introducing uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 2 retain their numerical results, including all 224 synthetic comparison values. V2 adds quantitative results for four real-world scenes and a blurry-scene result of 28.98 dB versus Deformable-3DGS's 24.19 dB (Figure 9). These are new evaluations, not same-setting gains over v1. Per-scene ablation entries are replaced by aggregate scores.

T1.justification: Equations 1–14 retain the same mathematical substance. Distinguishing estimated thresholds with a hat and expanding the event-count summation indices clarify notation rather than introduce new derivations or assumptions. Neither version contains formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The principal GTJM and DSD contribution claims persist. The dataset contribution is strengthened from a comprehensive dynamic-scene dataset to the claimed first event-inclusive 4D benchmark containing synthetic and real-world scenes, with state-of-the-art performance emphasized in the abstract and introduction.

C2.justification: V2 removes v1's explicit synthetic-only evaluation limitation and proposed future real-world collection, consistent with its added captured-data experiments. It also attributes the blurry-scene advantage to event-based deblurring. The central geometric-consistency and deformation-capacity explanations remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds substantial capture documentation: beam splitter, Prophesee Gen4, Basler ace, STM32 synchronization, rotating turntable, and frame-selection details. Conversely, it removes v1's implementation paragraph specifying PyTorch, random-point initialization, and the 7k threshold/47k joint-optimization budgets; the 3k static warm-up remains elsewhere. Both versions still promise future code and dataset release.

R1.justification: V2 expands benchmark novelty positioning and revises its discussion of prior datasets. It removes the dedicated Robust e-NeRF discussion while retaining that citation, and removes Structure-from-Motion Revisited with the initialization paragraph. Most other reference differences are renumbering or metadata updates.

P1.justification: V2 drops 'Fast' from the title, revises the abstract and experimental narrative, replaces 'intensity' with 'brightness,' and clarifies threshold notation. Comparisons gain quantitative, qualitative, and blurry-scene subheadings, but the overall section sequence and most method prose remain.

P2.justification: The experimental presentation is substantially reorganized through a new real-world results table and acquisition, real-world rendering, and blur figures. The synthetic comparison loses its Musicbox row, and the wide per-scene ablation table becomes a compact aggregate table. Existing diagnostic figures are largely retained but relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: V1 explicitly identifies synthetic-only validation as a limitation. V2 substantially addresses it with a documented capture setup and quantitative and qualitative comparisons on four real-world scenes (Table 3; Figures 6 and 8), strengthening evidence for practical applicability. The blur example provides additional support. Removed training details and reduced ablation granularity weaken reproducibility and diagnosis, but the real-sensor validation resolves an important deficiency.
